properties.name: MEADOW CREEK TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.
properties.description: This is a free trailhead site located 67 miles south of the town of Hungry Horse on the gravel East Side Reservoir Road #38. The trailhead is located at an elevation of 4,000 feet and is open from May 15 through November 30. Meadow Creek Trailhead is situated 100 feet above the Meadow Creek Gorge of the South Fork of the Flathead River. The 28 parking spots are divided into stock and foot use areas. The site is located in a second growth stand of trees. It is a high use site. It is mostly used as a major trailhead to access the Bob Marshall Wilderness on the Main East Side South Fork Trail #80. In the summer backpackers, stock users, and floaters access the wilderness. The trailhead is used for access to the early season and late season hunt in the wilderness from September 15 through late November. It also is used to access Picture Ridge Trail #107. A 60 foot long stock trail bridge crosses Meadow Creek Gorge 100 feet above the river and offers impressive views of the river. There are no tables or metal fire rings. There are vault toilets. There is no water on site, but water is available from a small creek crossing the road about 2 miles west further up the Meadow Creek Road. Water must be treated prior to consumption. Stock is allowed at the site. There are hitchrails, an unloading ramp, and feed bunks that stock may be tied to. Weed Seed Free Feed is required on all national forest lands. There is no garbage service and visitors need to plan to Pack It In, and Pack It Out. There is a food storage order in effect on all national forest land that requires that human and stock food, garbage, and other attractants be kept unavailable to bears. Your stay may not exceed 14 days. This is a remote location and there is no cell phone service in the area. The closest public phone is located 15 miles north at the Spotted Bear Ranger Station. Phone, gas, and food are located 67 miles north in the town of Hungry Horse.

properties.description: The former Eagle Creek Ranger Station is now available as a rental cabin. During that sametime the country wasexperiencing abooming gold rush. Dick Owen worked at Hassel in the mines and possibly at the Park mines. By the early 1900s, the Owens had moved to Radersburg, where Sarah Owen ran a boarding house. In 1905, the Elkhorn Forest Reserve was formed. In 1908, the Helena National Forest was designated and Eagle Cabin became an administrative site. The Eagle, Tizer and Glendale Stations were alllinked by a telephone line and connected tothe switchboard at a Radersburg store. The cabin is the oldest administrative log structure on the Helena National Forest and predates the establishment of the Forest. Eagle Station was used by the Forest Service on a regular basis until the early 1950s. Riders from the Crow and Indian Creek Livestock Association used the cabin over the years until the 1970s. Due to the historical value of Eagle Cabin,ithas been determined eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places. The current site consists of the cabin, a woodshed, toilet, barn, horse corrals, a fire ring, and is surrounded by a jackleg pole fence. There is no drinking water or electricity at the site. properties.description: This is a free trailhead site located 60 miles south of the town of Hungry Horse on the gravel East Side Reservoir Road #38. The trailhead is located at an elevation of 4,400 feet and is maintained from August 15 through November 15. South Creek Trailhead is situated next to South Creek. The 16 parking spots are next to the road. The site is located in a second growth stand of trees. It is a low use. It is used as a base for huckleberry picking in the summer and for the late season hunt in late October and November. It is used to access South Creek Trail #730 and Twin Creek Trail #237. There are no tables or metal fire rings. There is a vault toilet. There is no drinking water, but water is available from South Creek early in the season and must be treated prior to consumption. Stock is allowed at the site. There are hitchrails, and feed bunks that stock may be tied to. Weed Seed Free Feed is required on all national forest lands. There is no garbage service and visitors need to plan to Pack It In, and Pack It Out. There is a food storage order in effect on all national forest land that requires that human and stock food, garbage, and other attractants be kept unavailable to bears. Your stay may not exceed 14 days. This is a remote location and there is no cell phone service in the area. The closest public phone is located 6 miles west at the Spotted Bear Ranger Station. Phone, gas, and food are located 60 miles north in the town of Hungry Horse.

properties.description: Alta Campground features 15 campsites with 1 host site, drinking water, garbage, vault toilets, and handicap accessible picnic tables. Site will accept RVs or trailers to 30. Large yellow-barked Ponderosa Pine tower above many of the campsites which along with fir, aspen and lodgepole pine provide shade for many of the campsites. Painted Rocks Lake is located less than 5 miles away by paved road. Wildlife in the area include, bald eagle, mule and whitetail deer, moose, and elk along with numerous songbirds. Bighorn sheep can often be seen in the area. Sites can accommodate tents and/or RVs. Water is available at several locations within the campground. Attractions in the area include Horse Creek Hot Springs (about 18 miles on gravel road), historic ranger station (about 4 miles on paved road), and several scenic mountain peaks accessible by foot trail. Nearby Darby, MT (about 34 miles by paved road) is nearest full service city for all services (laundry, grocery store, etc.). properties.description: At approximately an 8000-foot elevation, Kings Hill Campground is the highest developed campground in the Little Belt Mountains. Kings Hill Campground generally opens in mid to late June and is the first to close in the fall around the end of September. The largest slot for a trailer is 35 feet in length. During fire season, nearby Porphyry Peak Lookout offers amazing views from the manned fire tower dating back to 1960. Visitors are welcome to go up into the Lookout if staff are available. properties.description: This recently relocated trailhead provides the shortest ? but steepest ? route to the district's highest point, Ch-Paa-Qn Peak. The Ch-Paa-Qn Peak Tr. No. 707 reaches the junction with Tr. No. 98.3 below the peak in 3 miles, but climbs over 2000 ft over that distance, plus almost 1000 feet more on the scramble to the summit. The upper 3 miles of Rd. No. 2178 were decommissioned in 2024, necessitating the relocation of this trailhead to its current location and the construction of about 3/4 of a mile of new trail. The new location greatly improves public access, although vehicles with low clearance are still not recommended on Rd. No. 2178. The trailhead features a large parking area and a hitching rail.

The trailhead features parking for about 8 vehicles.
